# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files and comment-only changes.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

## Why [#1121](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1121) was premature

It was filed against a version of the branch that never landed.

The title still carries its original premise: *"an old vendored pack still converges after the conversation surface was removed."* That was a real verify-in-production case — under the **second** reading of [#1114](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1114), the change retired the classification *together with the conversation surface it read* (`ctx.conversation()`, the transcript helper, the Stop hook's `transcript_path`). Removing an engine surface while members still hold an old vendored pack that calls it is exactly the old-pack/new-engine skew window that can only be proven once it converges in production. So filing a VIP issue for it was correct — for the artifact that was in flight at 15:04.

The branch was then rewritten to the **third** reading: pack-only. [PR #1118](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1118) merged at 15:20:36 with `additions: 4, deletions: 115` across 4 files — the check module, its `workRules` registration, its catalog row, its tests, plus a `packs/basics` version bump. The conversation surface is untouched, stated explicitly in the PR body. With the engine unchanged there is no skew window at all; a pack version bump is the ordinary nightly delivery path, and the nightly converge *is* the verification.

The timeline is the whole story:

| 14:24 | #1118 opened |
| 15:04:04 | #1121 filed — against the branch's *then-current* scope |
| 15:04:58 | queue item [#1122](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1122) created, `task:blocked` on #1118 |
| 15:16:20 | #1121 closed `not_planned`, body rewritten to the moot note |
| 15:20:36 | #1118 merged — pack-only |

So it wasn't a wrong judgment about verification, it was a VIP pass run against a mid-flight branch scope rather than against what actually landed. `verify-in-production` is meant to run at the *end* of a change, and "end" means the merged diff. A branch that gets rewritten twice invalidates any premise derived from its earlier states — the same failure mode the canon's own rule names: *returning to a branch that waited, re-verify the premise, unasked.*

## Why it closed keeping `claude-queued`

Because the close went straight to the issue instead of through the withdrawal lever. The bot's own comment names it: *"To withdraw the request before it starts, remove `claude-queued`."* Closing the issue doesn't strip the label, and stripping the label is the documented way to retract a queued request. Both were available; only the close happened.

**It's inert, though.** [`engine/scheduler/queue/tasks/implement-request/task.mjs:74`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/engine/scheduler/queue/tasks/implement-request/task.mjs#L74) checks issue state before the label:

```js
if (req.state !== 'open') return { run: false, reason: `issue #${req.number} was closed before this ran` };
if (!req.queued) { … }
```

The precondition is evaluated at pickup, not at queueing. #1122's not-before is `2026-08-22T06:00:00Z` and its blocker #1118 is merged, so it enters the queue on Aug 22, reads #1121 as closed, and self-declines with `run: false` — no sonnet session, no PR. The two guards are deliberately ordered so either one alone suffices; the label surviving costs one obsolete queue item converging, not a run.

The residue is cosmetic: a closed issue that still reads as queued to anyone scanning labels, and #1122 sitting open until Aug 22.

> ⚠️ Answered, nothing changed. Two loose ends if you want them tidied: `claude-queued` still on the closed [#1121](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1121), and [#1122](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1122) open until it self-declines on Aug 22. input.body:
The owner's call, from #1121: **a verification follow-up is never created before the PR has merged.** Sometimes PRs are rejected.

#1121 is the example. It was filed at 15:04 against the branch's then-current scope (a full retirement of the classification *and* the conversation surface, which really would have opened an old-pack/new-engine skew window). The branch was then rewritten to pack-only and #1118 merged at 15:20 with the conversation surface untouched. The verification's premise never existed in `main`. A human closed it by hand twelve minutes later.

## Why the current skill invites this

`packs/basics/skills/verify-in-production/SKILL.md` says it *"fires automatically at the end of a change"*, and `packs/basics/RULES.md:68` says to file it *"as part of finishing the change"*. A session that has written the code and opened the PR reads "the end of a change" as **now**.

The template then makes filing early the documented path: `Blocked-by: #<the change's PR>` (line 44) only makes sense if the PR is still open when you write it. That field exists to accommodate the premature file.

`packs/git-github/skills/merge-to-main/SKILL.md` already has it right — step 7, after the merge at step 4. The two entry points disagree.

## Why a rejected PR is worse than a wrong premise

`Blocked-by` waits on the blocker being **closed**. Nothing reads `merged`.

`engine/scheduler/queue/readiness.mjs:22`
```js
const blockersDone = blockedBy.every((n) => stateOf(n) === 'closed');
```

A rejected PR is `closed`, so it releases the item exactly as a merge does. What follows:

1. The item goes ready and runs.
2. It reads `In-production-when:` against an artifact that can never become true — the change never landed.
3. "Not yet live" → push `Not-before:` forward by `Retry-every:`, re-apply the labels, leave it open, and per the skill's line 87 post **no comment**: *"No comment; the bumped field is the record."*
4. Forever.

Nothing reclaims it:

- **Janitor rule A** (stale-ready, `janitor-rules.mjs:29`) cannot see it — it is sleeping on a future `Not-before`, never `task:ready`.
- **Janitor rule C** (stuck-dependency, `janitor-rules.mjs:67`) **explicitly exempts** it at line 72, `if (blockedBy.every((n) => stateOf(n) === 'closed')) return false;` — its own comment says *"Sleeping items (a future `Not-before`, blockers closed) never match: waiting for a time is the mechanism working."*

So a verification filed against a PR that gets rejected is a silent `sonnet` run every `Retry-every`, indefinitely, proving a change that does not exist. It is silent by design, which is what makes it hard to notice.

## The change

Move the trigger and remove the field that accommodated the early file:

- [ ] The skill fires **after the merge**, not at the end of the change — description, intro, and the `RULES.md:68` sentence.
- [ ] Drop `Blocked-by:` from the template and its bullet. Filed post-merge there is nothing to block on; `Not-before:` still does the real waiting. Nothing is ever in production before a merge, so there is no case where filing early is correct — a single structural answer means delete the field.
- [ ] State the rejected-PR case explicitly: a PR that closed unmerged files nothing.
- [ ] `merge-to-main` step 7 becomes the named trigger rather than one of two readings.
- [ ] Bump `packs/basics` and `packs/git-github`.

Out of scope, worth its own decision: whether the queue should refuse a work item whose `Blocked-by` names a PR that closed unmerged. That treats the symptom; if nothing is filed pre-merge the case cannot arise.

# Verify in production

A change is finished when someone has watched it work. Most changes you can watch **now**, and
that is the rule — this skill is only for the rest: a change whose proof lives somewhere the
repo cannot see yet. You are filing the proof, not doing the work — and the proof itself runs
unattended: an automatic check, end to end, with a person entering only where no automatic
check can exist.

## When it fires: after the merge, never before

**The PR must have merged.** This skill runs as a step of the merge, unasked — `merge-to-main`
calls it once the squash has landed — and at no other moment. Not when the code is written, not
when the PR opens, not while review is in flight.

The reason is that a PR can be **rejected**, and a branch that is still open can be rewritten
under you. Both leave a verification whose premise never reached `main`:

- A **rewritten branch** makes the brief describe a change that no longer exists. #1121 was filed
  against a scope its PR then dropped; the verification was moot before the merge it waited on.
- A **rejected PR** is worse, because the queue cannot tell it from a merge. A blocked item
  releases on its blocker being *closed*, and nothing reads `merged` — so the item goes ready,
  reads an `In-production-when:` that can never become true, pushes `Not-before:` forward by
  `Retry-every:` without comment, and repeats indefinitely. No janitor rule reclaims it: the
  stale-ready sweep cannot see an item sleeping on a future `Not-before`, and the
  stuck-dependency sweep exempts an item whose blockers have closed.

So there is no such thing as filing this early and letting the queue sort it out. Wait for the
merge, then read **what actually landed** — the merged diff, not the branch you remember writing.

## First: does this file anything at all?

Most changes **file nothing.** Run the test in this order and stop at the first answer:

1. **Did you watch it work in this session?** Then it is proven. File nothing.
2. **Did a test that ran prove it?** A unit test, a CI job, an executable-requirements or UI
   test covering exactly the behaviour that changed. File nothing — the suite is the mechanism
   that comes back.
3. **Does the change have an observable effect at all?** A comment, a design doc, a README, a
   rename with no behavioural edge, a refactor a passing suite already pins. File nothing.
4. **Otherwise: where does its effect first become observable?** If the answer is a place and a
   moment — a member repo once it converges, a site once it deploys, a session once it reloads
   its rules — that is what you file.

The bar is *could not be watched now*, not *would be nice to double-check*. A verification
filed for a change already covered by a test is a wasted run re-proving what the suite proved.

## What you file

**A deferred request** — the same ad-hoc lane `/do-later` rides, so the queue does the waiting,
the running and the lifecycle; nothing here adds machinery beside it. One issue, titled
`Verify in production: <the change, in a few words>`, its body the whole brief: the run that
verifies will never see this conversation and may be days away. Say what changed and why it
could not be watched now, then, each spelled verbatim on its own line:

```

Closes #1128.

Your call from #1121: **the follow-up is never created before the PR was merged, because sometimes PRs are rejected.**

Chasing that down turned up a worse failure than the moot issue you closed by hand.

## A rejected PR strands the verification forever

`Blocked-by` waits on its target being **closed**. Nothing reads `merged`.

`engine/scheduler/queue/readiness.mjs:22`
```js
const blockersDone = blockedBy.every((n) => stateOf(n) === 'closed');
```

A rejected PR is `closed`, so it releases the item exactly as a merge does. The item goes ready, reads an `In-production-when:` that can never become true, pushes `Not-before:` forward by `Retry-every:`, re-applies its labels, and posts **no comment** — the skill's own line 87 says *"No comment; the bumped field is the record."* Then it repeats.

Nothing reclaims it. Janitor rule A (`janitor-rules.mjs:29`) cannot see it, because it is sleeping on a future `Not-before` rather than sitting `task:ready`. Rule C (`janitor-rules.mjs:67`) **explicitly exempts** it at line 72 — its comment reads *"Sleeping items (a future `Not-before`, blockers closed) never match: waiting for a time is the mechanism working."*

So the cost of filing early is not a stale issue someone tidies up. It is a silent `sonnet` run every `Retry-every`, indefinitely, proving a change that does not exist. #1121 only escaped that because you closed it twelve minutes later.

## What changed

The skill fired *"automatically at the end of a change"*, and `RULES.md:68` said *"as part of finishing the change"* — which a session that has just opened its PR reads as **now**. Meanwhile `merge-to-main` step 7 already had it right, after the merge. Two entry points, disagreeing.

- **The trigger moves to the merge.** A new *"When it fires: after the merge, never before"* section, naming both ways an early file goes wrong: a rejected PR (above) and a branch rewritten under you (#1121, whose PR dropped the scope the verification was written against). It closes by telling the filer to read **what actually landed**, not the branch they remember writing.
- **`Blocked-by:` is gone from the template.** It was the accommodation for filing early, and it is the field that cannot distinguish a merge from a rejection. Filed post-merge there is nothing left to block on; `Not-before:` still does the real waiting. Nothing is ever in production before a merge, so there is no case where the early file is correct — a single structural answer, so the field goes rather than moves.
- **`merge-to-main` step 7 is named as the skill's only trigger**, so the two entry points can't drift apart again.

The contract is prose, so the assurance is the skill's own test. `packs/basics/verify-in-production.test.mjs` asserted `/Blocked-by:/` **must** be present — *"without the PR blocker the run races the merge"* — which is precisely the contract this inverts. `doesNotMatch(/^Blocked-by:/m)` is anchored to line-start deliberately: the prose still says the words "No `Blocked-by:`", and an unanchored pattern would pass on that sentence while the template field sat right above it.

Whether the queue should refuse a work item whose `Blocked-by` names a PR that closed unmerged. That treats the symptom; if nothing is filed pre-merge the case cannot arise. Noted at the bottom of #1128 rather than built here.
